content: 1. If platelet counts fall below 25 x 10^9/L and severe adverse reactions occur, reduce the dose by 50% or temporarily withhold treatment until the adverse reactions subside. If intolerance persists, discontinue treatment permanently. Regularly monitor liver function tests (LFTs), complete blood count (CBC), platelets, hemoglobin (Hgb), electrolytes, and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH). 2. When combining interferon alfa-2b with ribavirin, start with 3 million units/m² administered intramuscularly (IM) or subcutaneously (SC) three times per week for one week. Increase the dose to 6 million units/m² SC three times per week for 16–24 weeks, but do not exceed 10 million units per dose three times per week. Refer to the manufacturer’s package insert for dose adjustments. 3. Interferon alfa-2b increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Fezolinetant’s area under the curve (AUC) and peak plasma concentration are elevated when co-administered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. 4. Avoid using deferiprone with other drugs associated with neutropenia or agranulocytosis. If no alternative is available, monitor the absolute neutrophil count more frequently. 5. Palifermin increases the toxicity of interferon alfa-2b. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Palifermin should not be administered within 24 hours before, during, or after the infusion of antineoplastic agents, as co-administration within this timeframe has been associated with increased severity and duration of oral mucositis. 6. Pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity. Avoid co-administration of pexidartinib with other hepatotoxic agents. Monitor liver function closely if these drugs are used together. 7. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid, during pretomanid therapy. 8. Ropinterferon alfa-2b and interferon alfa-2b can cause additive myelosuppression. Avoid co-administration and monitor patients closely for excessive myelosuppression. 9. Interferon alfa-2b and hydroxyurea may cause cutaneous vasculitic toxicities, such as vasculitic ulcerations and gangrene, particularly in patients with a history of or currently receiving interferon therapy. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Interferon alfa-2b and lamivudine increase the risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor liver function closely. 11. Siponimod and interferon alfa-2b both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution during co-administration and in the weeks following therapy. Consider the half-life and mechanism of action of these drugs when switching therapies to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 12. Interferon alfa-2b increases the levels of theophylline by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution, especially in smokers, as they may have a greater risk of interaction. 13. Tobramycin (inhaled) and interferon alfa-2b both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to reduce the risk of ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely if co-administration is necessary. 14. Ublituximab and interferon alfa-2b both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider the duration of effect and mechanism of action of these therapies if co-administered. 15. Interferon alfa-2b increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Interferon alfa-2b increases the levels of zidovudine by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Shark cartilage and interferon alfa-2b may theoretically enhance anti-angiogenesis through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 18. Weight loss and growth inhibition have been reported in pediatric patients receiving combination therapy with interferon alfa-2b. Long-term growth inhibition (height) has been observed in some patients. 19. Peripheral neuropathy has been observed when interferon alfa-2b is used in combination with telbivudine. 20. There is a risk of visual impairment and retinal disorders with interferon alfa-2b. Discontinue treatment if ophthalmologic problems develop. 21. Use interferon alfa-2b with caution in patients with endocrine disorders, such as thyroid disease or diabetes mellitus prone to ketoacidosis. 22. Avoid using interferon alfa-2b in patients with pre-existing cardiac abnormalities, advanced cancer, or rapidly progressive AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma. 23. Discontinue interferon alfa-2b if acute hypersensitivity reactions occur. 24. Interferon alfa-2b may exacerbate pre-existing psoriasis and sarcoidosis or lead to the development of new sarcoidosis. 25. Ensure patients are well-hydrated during initial treatment with interferon alfa-2b. 26. If platelet counts are below 50,000/mm³, avoid intramuscular administration; subcutaneous administration may be used instead. 27. Do not use the 18 million IU or 50 million IU powder for injection or the 18 million IU multidose vial for condylomata acuminata. 28. Interferon alfa-2b increases the risk of hepatic decompensation and death in patients with cirrhosis. Monitor liver function closely during treatment, and discontinue therapy if liver function abnormalities develop. 29. Numerous cardiotoxicities, including arrhythmias, ischemia, infarction, and cardiomyopathy, have been reported during and immediately after interferon alfa-2b infusion. 30. Interferon alfa-2b is classified as Pregnancy Category C. There is no evidence of fetal risk in controlled studies in pregnant women. The effects on lactation are unknown.
